pl-l4d31c4-d1e115.summary: Asks when those who procure abortion are judged murderers.

pl-l4d31c4-d1e118.summary: Answers with Augustine on Exodus that the fetus pertains to homicide when it is formed and has a soul; the law did not want the unformed fetus, without a living soul, to count as homicide.
claims: Abortion of an unformed fetus is not homicide.

pl-l4d31c4-d1e130.summary: Adds Augustine: the unformed fetus has no soul, so it is punished by a fine, not life for life; the soul is given to the already formed body, not born with the seed, for otherwise many souls would perish daily when seed comes to nothing; the house must be built before the inhabitant enters.
claims: The soul is infused into the formed body.
The soul is not transmitted with the seed.

pl-l4d31c4-d1e140.summary: Cites Jerome: seeds are gradually formed in the womb, and it is not counted homicide until the elements take shape and members.
claims: It is homicide once the fetus has form and members.

pl-l4d31c4-d1e149.summary: Concludes that those who procure abortion are murderers when the fetus is formed and ensouled.
claims: Abortion of a formed fetus is homicide.

pl-l4d31c4.summary: Asks when those who procure abortion are judged murderers. Augustine on Exodus: the unformed fetus without a living soul is not counted homicide, the law fining rather than exacting life for life; the soul is given to the formed body, not derived with the seed, else many souls would perish daily. Jerome: it is not homicide until the elements take shape and members. So procuring abortion is homicide when the fetus is formed and ensouled.
claims: Abortion is homicide once the fetus is formed and ensouled.
The soul is infused into the formed body, not transmitted with the seed.
